invite_link.hint: Whoever gets it opens the link, picks a name and asks to join. Then it's up to you to open the door: an invite doesn't let anyone in on its own.
invite_link.intro: Here is the link to send. It appears only now: the instance keeps a fingerprint of it, not the code.
invite_link.local_only: This link points to {{host}}, which can only be reached from here. Open the instance from its address on your home network — the one you see in the NAS panel — and create the invite again from there.
invite_link.local_only_this_computer: This link points to this computer, which can only be reached from here. Open the instance from its address on your home network — the one you see in the NAS panel — and create the invite again from there.
join.display_name_hint: What people should call you. You can change it whenever you like.
join.error_invalid_invite: This invite is not valid: it may have expired, been used already or been withdrawn.
join.error_username_taken: This username is already taken. Choose another one.
join.message: A couple of lines about you
join.message_hint: Read by whoever decides whether to let you in.
join.message_placeholder: I live on the second floor, staircase B.
join.sent.body: You asked to join {{instance}}. Now it's up to the people who run the instance: once they approve you, you can sign in with the username and password you just chose.
join.sent.note: An invite alone doesn't get you in: a person always has to open the door for you.
join.sent.title: Request sent
join.title: Ask to join
join.username_hint: Lowercase, no spaces. This one can't be changed.
login.error_credentials: Username or password is not valid.
login.forgot: Forgot your password? <link>Use your recovery code</link>
recover.code_hint: Capitals, lowercase and dashes don't matter: type it the way you copied it.
recover.done.body: The code you used is now spent. This is its replacement, and once again this is the only time it is shown.
recover.done.sessions: For your safety, every open session has been closed: you'll need to sign in again on each device.
recover.done.sessions_counted: For your safety, every open session has been closed ({{count}}): you'll need to sign in again on each device.
recover.done.title: Password reset
recover.error_invalid: Username or recovery code is not valid.
recover.intro: It's the code you were shown when the instance was created, or after your last recovery.
recover.title: Get back in with your recovery code
restore.body: The keys to your private messages are created in the browser and stay there, so this one — new, or emptied — doesn't have yours. But there is a copy on the instance: your passphrase opens it and puts the same key back here, so you rejoin your conversations in place of your previous browser.
restore.error: This passphrase doesn't open the copy. Try again.
restore.history: Your history comes back as soon as another person in each conversation opens it again: by opening it, they hand you back the key to read it.
restore.skip_note: If you continue without them, this browser makes a key of its own: you still rejoin your conversations, but your previous browser stays in them as one more of your devices. Putting the key back replaces it instead. The copy is not deleted.
restore.title: Your keys are not on this browser
